open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request input contract for instance selection detail
open_points.kind: missing input needed for required error split
open_points.text: "Inputs: A ManifestOperation M10 with instance facts ..." + "Enforces ... no selected instance (no name), no `api_base_url` (a name without one) ..." + check_binding_current output "The current ManifestOperation M10 — and beside it, not in it, the selected instance's name"
open_points.question: How does `service_invoker.prepare_request` receive the selected instance name so it can deterministically distinguish `instance_not_selected` from `instance_address_missing`?
options: Add selected instance name (optional) as an explicit input to `prepare_request`
Make `prepare_request` infer from ManifestOperation field absence (collapsing the distinction)
Move the distinction entirely to `bindings.check_binding_current` and have `prepare_request` receive a normalized pre-send instance status
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit selected-instance-name input and keep both detail codes distinct.

open_points.subject: MCP read_spooled_file call path
open_points.text: MCP catalogue row: "`read_spooled_file` | owner | `store.read_value_bytes`" versus later: "Checks run in that order ... then the record's existence, through `store.read_records`; then whether its run holds its spool, from `runs.read_run`; only then are the bytes read through `store.read_value_bytes`."
open_points.question: Is `read_spooled_file` defined as only a direct `store.read_value_bytes` call, or as a multi-call sequence with mandatory existence and spool-hold checks before reading bytes?
options: Treat catalogue `calls` column as exhaustive (single call only)
Treat prose as normative (must call `store.read_records` then `runs.read_run` then `store.read_value_bytes`)
open_points.default_guess: Treat the detailed prose as normative and implement the 3-step check sequence.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances service iteration scope
open_points.text: "Errors: `refused` naming the first failing service, services taken in `service_id` code-point order and each one's manifest record read in its turn"
open_points.question: Which set of services must `check_installed_instances` iterate: all services in installation config, only services with a selected instance, or some other set?
options: All services present in installation service configuration (including those with no selected instance)
Only services with a selected instance
Only services that also have credential configuration
open_points.default_guess: Only services with a selected instance, since unselected services are explicitly allowed and not invocable.
